content:
What is QuickStark.Ai and how does it work?

Describe the product you want in plain language and QuickStark.Ai builds it - the screens people see, the backend behind them, the database underneath and the sign-in flow, ready to go live. Web and mobile come out of the same description.

QuickStark.Ai positions itself as: "Build Full-Stack Web & Mobile Apps in Minutes with one cohesive platform for product generation, infrastructure, and launch-ready workflows."

What do I actually end up with when QuickStark.Ai finishes a build?

A product that runs, not a mockup or a pile of screens to hand off. You get the pages people use, the database behind them, sign-in already wired up and real code underneath - live on a URL you can share the same day, and still yours to keep changing.

metadata.title: What you actually end up with

content:
What can I build with QuickStark.Ai?

Anything with a front end and something running behind it: customer-facing web and mobile apps, dashboards, marketplaces, booking and subscription products, internal tools. If it needs pages, accounts, data and payments, it is in range.

Do I need coding experience to use QuickStark.Ai?

No. You describe what you want in ordinary words and QuickStark.Ai does the building. What it writes underneath is real Next.js and React code, so if you bring in a developer later there is something familiar for them to pick up.

Can QuickStark.Ai build both web and mobile apps?

Yes - "Build web and mobile apps" is one of the three core capabilities. Turn a single prompt into production interfaces - Next.js 15, React 19 and Tailwind components that fit every screen and deploy the moment they compile. Web and mobile come out of the same description.

Does QuickStark.Ai build the backend as well as the front end?

Yes - "Build secure backends" is one of the three core capabilities. Everything behind the scenes is handled for you: somewhere safe to keep your data, checks that stop bad data getting in, and sign-ins that work from day one - on Supabase, Postgres or Firebase.

What are AI agents and workflows in QuickStark.Ai?

"Build AI agents and workflows" is one of the three core capabilities. Agents are the parts of your product that keep working when you are not. They watch for events, run jobs in the background, remember what matters between sessions, and can take payments. You describe the job once and they handle it from then on.

What exactly can QuickStark.Ai generate from a natural-language description?

Instantly generate native mobile applications, progressive web apps, production APIs, schema-perfect databases, authentication architectures, AI agents, secure cloud storage, and fully automated deployment configurations using simple natural language.

metadata.title: Full list of what can be generated

content:
Where does my data live, and what does QuickStark.Ai connect to?

Your data sits on Supabase, Postgres or Firebase - whichever you prefer - with sign-ins wired up from the start. Beyond that, your app can reach the rest of your stack through webhooks and take payments through Stripe.

content:
How do I sign in or create a QuickStark.Ai account?

Sign-up and sign-in are offered through Google, Facebook, Apple and GitHub, or with an email address and password, or with a phone number that receives a one-time SMS code. Choosing email sign-up may require confirming your address: a link is sent to your inbox and opening it signs you in.

How much does QuickStark.Ai cost?

There are three plans:
- Free - $0/month. A simple starting point to explore QuickStark.Ai and validate your first product ideas.
- Standard - $25/month. The most balanced plan for serious builders shipping polished web and mobile experiences.
- Pro - $150/month. A high-touch tier for advanced teams orchestrating larger systems and more complex launches.

Billing is monthly, or annual for 20% less. Every paid plan card carries its own annual switch, so plans can be priced yearly one at a time.

What do I get on the Free plan?

Free costs $0/month and includes:
- 5 daily build credits
- Unlimited sandbox iteration
- Publishing from 50 credits - top up or upgrade to go live
- Standard community support

The Free plan does not include custom domains or private repositories. Because daily credits do not roll over, a Free account cannot accumulate the 50 credits a first publish costs - going live requires a top-up or an upgrade.

What do I get on the Standard plan?

Standard costs $25/month and includes:
- 100 credits per month, plus the daily allowance of 5 credits
- Private repositories and custom domains
- Unused credits roll over one billing cycle
- GitHub integration
- Priority support

What do I get on the Pro plan?

Pro costs $150/month and includes:
- 600 credits per month, plus the daily allowance of 5 credits
- Private repositories and custom domains
- Unused credits roll over one billing cycle
- Priority support

Is there a discount for paying yearly?

Yes. Annual billing saves 20% against the monthly rate, charged twelve months at a time. Each paid plan card carries its own annual switch, so you can price one plan yearly while comparing the others at their monthly rate.

Is there more than one place to see QuickStark.Ai pricing?

Yes. The landing page has a pricing section at quickstark.tech/#pricing, and there is a standalone pricing page at quickstark.tech/pricing. Both quote the same three plans at the same prices - Free at $0, Standard at $25 and Pro at $150 a month - and use the same plan names, so a customer comparing the two pages should not see a discrepancy. The annual switch and the per-plan feature lists appear on the landing page section rather than the standalone page.

metadata.title: Where pricing is shown on the site

content:
How do QuickStark.Ai credits work?

Credits are the unit everything is billed in. Every account receives a daily allowance of 5 credits, and paid plans add a monthly grant on top (100 on Standard, 600 on Pro).

Credits are spent expiring-soonest-first: today's daily grant, then last cycle's rollover, then this cycle's grant, then top-ups. Top-up credits are spent last because they are the only credits that never expire.

What is the daily credit allowance and does it roll over?

Every account gets 5 daily build credits, on every plan including Free. Daily credits are explicitly non-rolling - an unused day is gone. Monthly credits on Standard and Pro are different: those roll over for one billing cycle.

What does it cost to publish or redeploy a project?

Taking a project live for the first time costs 50 credits. Every deploy after that costs 1 credit.

Publishing is charged as a flat fee, not metered. The first publish is expensive because provisioning is the expensive part - a repository, a subdomain, hosting - and it happens once per project. Redeploys are deliberately nominal so that iterating on a live app stays cheap.

Can I buy more credits if I run out mid-month?

Yes. A top-up pack is 50 credits for $10. Top-up credits are the only credits with no expiry date, which is also why they are spent last - the system uses expiring credits first so you do not burn credits you paid for while free ones expire unused.

Do I get any free credits when I sign up?

Yes. Every new account opens with 10 credits at no charge. At the top-up pack's rate of 50 credits for $10, that is about two dollars' worth.

How many credits does each kind of action use?

- Pure chat / planning: 0 to 1 credit. Low-overhead conversational prompts, error troubleshooting, and architecture planning.
- Code generation / file editing: 0.5 to 2.5 credits. Variable cost based on output token length and scope of file modifications.
- Production publishing / deploy: 1 to 50 credits. 50 credits to take a project live the first time, then 1 for each deploy after that.
- Runtime cloud / database sync: 0 credits. Covered by base plan allowances; heavy background traffic scales with tier limits rather than drawing from the credit pool.

metadata.title: What each action costs in credits

content:
What URL is my published project served from?

Published projects are served from a subdomain of quickstark.tech by default. Custom domains are available on the Standard and Pro plans; the Free plan does not include them.

Do I get a private repository, and is there GitHub integration?

Private repositories are included on the Standard and Pro plans. The Free plan does not include private repositories. GitHub integration is listed as a Standard plan feature and carries through to Pro.

What level of support does my plan include?

- Free: standard community support.
- Standard: priority support.
- Pro: priority support.

Where do I find things on the QuickStark.Ai site?

The main navigation links to Features, Workflow, Pricing and FAQ. The footer groups links under Product (Features, Pricing, Get Started), Company (About, Contact, Careers), Legal (Terms of Service at /terms, Privacy Policy at /privacy) and Social (GitHub, X, Twitter, Slack).

Note for support agents: at the time of capture the Company and Social footer links were placeholders that did not yet point to real destinations, and the "Workflow" nav item had no matching section on the page. Do not promise a customer these links work.

A customer says sign-in does nothing, or reports that authentication is unavailable. What is happening?

Two known causes:

1. Authentication is disabled for the deployment because its Supabase environment variables are not configured. The site renders normally but sign-in cannot work. The fix is on the operator side: set NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in the deployment environment and redeploy. A redeploy is required - restarting is not enough, because the values are read at build time as well as at runtime.

2. The origin the customer is signing in from is not on the Supabase Redirect URLs allowlist. This fails after the customer has already approved the provider, so it reads to them as "sign-in did nothing". Each origin needs its callback path registered.

metadata.title: Sign-in is unavailable or does nothing

content:
A customer signed up with email but was not signed in. Why?

When email confirmation is enabled, sign-up does not return a session. The customer is told to check their inbox: "Almost there - confirm your email. We sent a link to <address>; opening it signs you in." Opening that link establishes the session and forwards them to the dashboard. If confirmation is disabled, sign-up returns a session immediately and goes straight to the dashboard.
